content.comment_body: Hello, I have a [company_name] Field PC with Intel Core i7-8850H and successive upgrades from [product_name] 6.0 to [product_name] 8.3 and 8.2. With [product_name] 8.3, I encounter significant delays when starting, stopping, or opening/closing projects—the software becomes unresponsive for several minutes but does not crash. This issue does not occur with [product_name] 8.2. My PC also has [product_name] [version_no] installed. Any suggestions? Thank you.

[product_name] 8.3 has grown much larger and slower, likely due to AWS integration. Except for AWS features, it works similarly to previous versions for programming. Personally, I avoid AWS, develop with [product_name] 8.2.1, and only use 8.3 to upload to compatible devices. Best regards, [user_name] (translated using Google).

In my experience, it’s not as severe. I also don’t use AWS, and my [product_name] 8.3 runs fine. When transferring programs between PC and [product_name], version 8.3.x operates slightly slower than 8.2.x, but not drastically.

Hello, This is quite frustrating, especially since it occurs on a [company_name] Field PC with an i7-8850H, 32GB RAM, and all legitimate software. I suspect it’s not due to program size, but possibly background updates or similar processes. Developing in 8.2 and uploading with 8.3 is manageable, but I am working on a MODBUS application and need to upload frequently, as the simulator cannot fully test communication. My device firmware is 1.83, so I rely on [product_name] 8.3. It’s odd that [company_name] appears unaware of the issue. For example, clicking 'Options' results in the software hanging for minutes.

Hello, I have identified the issue: a missing UDF could not be cancelled within the software, causing it to hang. By deleting the .[product_name]8.3 folder from the user directories, everything started working correctly. Thanks for your support!

I also have a missing UDF entry, but my program does not hang when changing options. Try this method: navigate to your Windows system user directory and locate the .[product_name]8.3 folder, where you’ll find a .properties file. Open it with Notepad. If you see the missing UDF entry, create a 'test' directory and move the file there. Restart [product_name] and check options again. Regards, [user_name]

Within the options menu, under 'UDF' for the UDF library, use 'Add directory' to specify the folder where your UDFs are stored on your PC. [product_name] only searches for required UDFs in directories that you specifically list there.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are experiencing long delays and program hangs using [product_name] 8.3 on high-performance [company_name] Field PCs, especially during startup, shutdown, or project transitions. The main cause appears related to missing User Defined Function (UDF) entries, triggering configuration sensitivity and software lag. Solutions involve removing the configuration folder linked to [product_name] 8.3, which resolves performance issues, indicating that the software is highly affected by missing or incorrect file references.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [product_name] 8.3 to function smoothly—opening, closing, and navigating options quickly on advanced hardware and up-to-date software—without unexplained delays or program hangs.
